ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, $P$ is a point on line segment $MN$, and $Q$ is the midpoint of line segment $PN$. If $MN = 10$ and $MP = 6$, what is the length of $MQ$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $MN = 10$ and $MP = 6$, \\
it follows that $NP = MN - MP = 4$, \\
because point Q is the midpoint of NP, \\
it follows that $PQ = QN = \frac{1}{2} NP = 2$, \\
thus $MQ = MP + PQ = 6 + 2 = \boxed{8}$.
